fn.IIf: Returns the second value if the condition is true, the third one otherwise.
fn.Nz: Replaces a Null value with a substitute (zero or an empty string by default).
fn.IsNull: Tells whether the value is Null.
fn.IsNumeric: Tells whether the value can be read as a number.
fn.IsDate: Tells whether the value can be read as a date.
fn.Len: Returns the number of characters in a text.
fn.Left: Returns the first characters of a text.
fn.Right: Returns the last characters of a text.
fn.Mid: Extracts part of a text starting at a position.
fn.Trim: Removes the spaces at the start and end of a text.
fn.LTrim: Removes the spaces at the start of a text.
fn.RTrim: Removes the spaces at the end of a text.
fn.UCase: Converts a text to upper case.
fn.LCase: Converts a text to lower case.
fn.InStr: Returns the position of one text inside another, or 0 if absent.
fn.Replace: Replaces each occurrence of a text with another one.
fn.Space: Returns a text made of the requested number of spaces.
fn.String: Repeats a character the requested number of times.
fn.StrComp: Compares two texts and returns -1, 0 or 1.
fn.Format: Formats a value using a named or custom format.
fn.Round: Rounds a number to the requested decimals (banker's rounding).
fn.Int: Returns the integer part of a number, rounded down.
fn.Fix: Returns the integer part of a number by dropping the decimals.
fn.Abs: Returns the absolute value of a number.
fn.Sgn: Returns the sign of a number: -1, 0 or 1.
fn.Sqr: Returns the square root of a number.
fn.Val: Reads the leading digits of a text and returns the matching number.
fn.CInt: Converts a value to an integer.
fn.CLng: Converts a value to a long integer.
fn.CDbl: Converts a value to a floating-point number.
fn.CDate: Converts a value to a date.
fn.Now: Returns the current date and time.
fn.Year: Returns the year of a date.
fn.Month: Returns the month of a date (1 to 12).
fn.Day: Returns the day of the month of a date.
fn.Hour: Returns the hour of a date and time value (0 to 23).
fn.Minute: Returns the minutes of a date and time value.
fn.Second: Returns the seconds of a date and time value.
fn.Weekday: Returns the day of the week of a date (1 for Sunday).
fn.DateAdd: Adds an interval (days, months, years...) to a date.
fn.DateDiff: Computes the number of intervals between two dates.
fn.DatePart: Returns a part of a date (year, quarter, week...).
fn.DateSerial: Builds a date from a year, a month and a day.
fn.TimeSerial: Builds a time from hours, minutes and seconds.
fn.Sum: Returns the sum of the values in the group.
fn.Avg: Returns the average of the values in the group.
fn.Count: Returns the number of non-Null values in the group; Count(*) counts the records.
fn.Min: Returns the smallest value in the group.
fn.Max: Returns the largest value in the group.
fn.First: Returns the value of the first record in the group.
fn.Last: Returns the value of the last record in the group.
fn.StDev: Returns the standard deviation of the values in the group (sample).
fn.StDevP: Returns the standard deviation of the values in the group (population).
fn.Var: Returns the variance of the values in the group (sample).
fn.VarP: Returns the variance of the values in the group (population).

split.title: Database Splitter
split.intro: This wizard moves the tables of the current database to a new data file, preferably placed on a shared network drive. The current database becomes a front-end application linked to those tables: each workstation can then use its own copy of the front-end. A backup copy of the database is made before the split.
split.done: Database successfully split. Data file: {{path}}. Backup copy: {{backup}}.
split.noTables: This database contains no local table to move.

migrate.title: Move to Server Wizard
migrate.intro: This wizard moves every local table of the current database to a PostgreSQL or SQL Server database, with its data, keys, indexes and relationships, then replaces them by linked tables of the same names. A backup copy of the database is made first. Validation rules and calculated default values stay in the application, which becomes a front-end application.
